Mayyun Island: a discreet strategic chokepoint at the heart of major rivalries in the Red Sea Mayyun Island, located at the heart of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, is now emerging as a pivotal node in the strategic rivalries shaping the Red Sea. This volcanic outcrop is drawing increasing attention from regional and international powers due to its capacity to control, or disrupt, one of the world’s most critical maritime trade routes. Since early April, several Western intelligence services have requested satellite imagery acquisitions from Airbus Defence and Space, specifically targeting Mayyun. This renewed interest comes amid heightened tensions between anti-Houthi factions, particularly between the internationally recognized Yemeni government (backed by Riyadh) and forces affiliated with Tareq Saleh, nephew of Ali Abdullah Saleh. Long supported by Abu Dhabi, Tareq Saleh is now attracting Washington’s attention, signaling a possible realignment of external backing. A revealing episode illustrates these frictions: on April 1, military transport aircraft reportedly attempted to land on the island but were prevented from doing so by pro-Saudi forces. While this account was officially denied, OSINT analyses nevertheless confirmed the suspicious passage, the previous evening, of an Ilyushin Il-76 (registration TL-ATD), which circled above Mayyun before heading back toward Africa. The aircraft is operated by Invicta Air Cargo, a Central African company with structural ties to Emirati security networks, notably through Gewan Holding, which is close to Hamdan bin Zayed al-Nahyan, brother of President Mohammed bin Zayed al-Nahyan. Technical connections between the two entities (including the reuse of digital infrastructure and transfers of aviation assets) suggest operational continuity. Notably, a few days after flying over Mayyun, the aircraft traveled from Fujairah to the Israeli Nevatim airbase, pointing to broader, and potentially coordinated, logistical circuits. On the ground, the control dynamics over the island have evolved. Initially, Abu Dhabi had been developing discreet air infrastructure there, progress of which was still visible in commercial satellite imagery in 2025. However, since early 2026, the UAE appears to have withdrawn. This shift is part of a broader reassertion of control by Riyadh over local forces (notably those of the Southern Transitional Council), thereby consolidating its direct influence. Currently, control of Mayyun rests on a combination of Tareq Saleh’s forces and a significant Saudi contingent, particularly deployed around the island’s airstrip. However, the aforementioned aerial incident suggests that coordination between these actors remains imperfect, if not openly strained. Moreover, several local sources indicate a deepening of security cooperation between Saudi Arabia, the United States, and Israel on the island. Narratives disseminated by the Houthis had already, as early as February, pointed to joint projects aimed at transforming Mayyun into a forward strategic platform. The objective appears clear: to establish a foothold capable of containing, or countering, any attempt by the Iran-backed Houthis to blockade the strait, echoing recurring tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Finally, the gradual withdrawal of the UAE from its insular positions in Yemen (notably Socotra and Mayyun) now seems nearly complete. According to several security sources, their last active foothold would be Abd al-Kuri Island in the Indian Ocean, marking a strategic repositioning in response to Saudi Arabia’s growing assertiveness. In sum, Mayyun stands out as a true geostrategic chokepoint, where intra-coalition rivalries, shifting alliances, and power projection dynamics converge. Control over this small island far exceeds its size: it directly shapes the security balance of a maritime corridor that is vital on a global scale.

We mourn the passing of Prof Raphael Munavu, a distinguished scholar and steadfast public servant, whose life’s work elevated the cause of education and national development. His enduring commitment to learning and public service leaves a profound legacy that will continue to inspire generations. In recognition of his leadership and experience, I appointed him in September 2022 to chair the Presidential Working Party on Education Reform, one of his final major public assignments. Under his stewardship, the Working Party widely engaged stakeholders across sectors and delivered thoughtful and forward-looking recommendations to review the Competency-Based Curriculum and align our education system to evolving needs of our nation. I also appointed Prof Munavu chairperson of Konza Technopolis board of directors, where he did a sterling job in positioning the organisation as Africa's Silicon Savannah. As we honour his legacy, we recommit ourselves to advancing his vision of an education system that is equitable, innovative, and responsive to the aspirations of our people. I extend my sincere condolences, and those of the entire nation, to Prof Munavu’s family, friends and colleagues in academia during this time of loss.

🎶 On 23 April 2026, the Embassy of Russia in Norway hosted a spring musical salon marking the 135th anniversary of the birth of the great Russian composer Sergei Prokofiev, attended by members of the diplomatic corps, compatriots and Norwegian guests. The concert featured Sergei Prokofiev’s Sonata for Cello and Piano in C major, composed in 1949 for the renowned Soviet cellist Mstislav Rostropovich. The evening at the Embassy also featured the world premiere of the Sonata for Cello and Piano ‘Beksinski’ and works from the collection ‘Tableaux féeriques’ by the renowned Norwegian composer Martin Romberg, who personally introduced his music. These unique masterpieces of classical music were performed by outstanding musicians from Luxembourgб cellist Dmitry Maslennikov and pianist Sabina Weyer. The Ambassador of Russia to Norway Nikolay Korchunov emphasised the particular significance of Sergei Prokofiev’s music in terms of fostering intercultural dialogue between our countries in the current challenging international circumstances, and thanked Martin Romberg, Dmitry Maslennikov and Sabina Weyer for their contribution to this important mission.

Il 25 Aprile ho sempre festeggiato la liberazione dal nazifascismo. Non oggi che sono Ministro. Lo festeggiavo già da giovane sindaco del mio comune nel 1991, ricevendo dallo storico Presidente ANPI locale, il Geom. Giovanni Ghigo, socialista del PSI, ex partigiano, la tessera onoraria, ogni anno. La numero 1 era riservata al Sindaco da sempre. Anche nei 5 anni nei quali il Sindaco era stato il figlio dell’ex Podestà. Erano anni nei quali nell’Anpi c’erano i partigiani veri, quelli che avevano combattuto, quelli che avevano rischiato la vita. Quella tessera era qualcosa di importante, vero, serio, perché era un pezzo di storia vissuta . Mai a nessuno di loro sarebbe venuto in mente di allontanare dalla cerimonia, che facevamo davanti al municipio, la bandiera di qualcuno che stava combattendo per la propria libertà, come avevano fatto loro. Perché loro declinavano la parola Liberazione in senso universale: la liberazione italiana dal nazifascismo come pezzo della lotta più grande di tutta l’umanità contro la violenza, la sopraffazione, la follia della guerra, l’ingiustizia, l’invasione. Mai nessuno di loro avrebbe mancato di rispetto alla storia della Brigata Ebraica che era stata al loro fianco a combattere. Quelli però erano Uomini veri, persone vere, con valori veri, che avevano vissuto la Resistenza e credevano nella Giustizia e nei valori fondanti della Repubblica, non intollerante ed illiberale gentaglia come quella che abbiamo visto all’opera per reprimere la libertà di espressione: Ieri gente che forse non ha mai combattuto per altro che non fosse il proprio interesse individuale ha sputato sullo spirito del 25 aprile, senza nemmeno capirlo, senza rendersene conto. Hanno mancato di rispetto agli Uomini ed alle Donne che hanno perso la vita nella Resistenza perché chiunque potesse manifestare la propria idea in libertà, perché gli invasori fossero respinti, perché la violenza e la forza bruta trovassero chi aveva il coraggio di fermarle. Mi spiace per queste “persone” ma ci sarà sempre gente che invece continuerà a combattere e morire per la libertà e la giustizia, nonostante quello che persone come loro continueranno a fare per prevaricare.

The prayer was led by Shaykh Syed Nehmat Ali Shah, Imam of Central Jamaat-e-Ahl-e-Sunnat. Following the Friday prayer, Shaykh-ul-Islam delivered nasiha (words of wisdom) to the gathering. His Eminence Shaykh ul Islam emphasized how faith can become a natural part of a child’s inner being when the proper environment is created to nurture this development from within. The Qur’an describes religion as part of human nature; however, Shaykh-ul-Islam explained that this innate nature must be activated through conscious choices. Shaykh ul Islam highlighted that parents carry a special responsibility to create an environment in which faith can grow. Faith does not develop in isolation—it must be awakened. Just as a child naturally learns to cry, faith too is innate within human beings. Without the right environment, a person may lose their identity—like a lion raised among goats. Therefore, children must be nurtured through positive surroundings from an early stage, even before birth. His Eminence further stated that the character of parents plays a decisive role, as children are influenced by what they see and hear. Respect, calmness, and positive attitudes are therefore essential in shaping a child’s personality. In his concluding message to the public, Shaykh-ul-Islam advised focusing on the good in others and striving to improve oneself, as this strengthens both a child’s character and faith. We extend our gratitude to Zahid Aslam, Chairman of Central Jamaat-e-Ahl-e-Sunnat, Shaykh Syed Nehmat Ali Shah, Imam of Central Jam-e Masjid Ahl-e-Sunnat, and Mufti Zubair Tabassum for their hospitality and warm reception. Representatives from MQI Norway were also present, including Imam and Director MQI Norway Allama Muhammad Iqbal Fani, Afzal Ansari (Ameer-e-Tehreek), Awais Ejaz Ahmed (President MQI), Hassan Bashir (General Secretary MQI), Pervaiz Nisar (Head, House of Representatives MQI), Arfan Ansari (President MQI Oslo), Asif Javed (President Minhaj Cultural Center Kløfta), and Shafique Siddique (President Minhaj Cultural Center Drammen).

🤯 Results of the UAV attack on the Tuapse tank farm in Krasnodar Krai: 🔴 Destroyed – 24 tanks, or 52%; 🟠 Damaged – 4 tanks, or 9%; 🟢 Undamaged – 18 tanks, or 39%; In total, 61% of the storage tanks will not be operational in the near future in one way or another. Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) Tuapse, April 26🔥 The consequences of a drone attack on the sanctions component of Russia - the tank farm of the Tuapse Refinery. From the available high-quality satellite image, it can be concluded that a significant part of the tank farm has been damaged or destroyed. It's worth noting that the territory of the refinery itself remained without visible damage. ❓ It's up to the specialized experts to analyze in detail what exactly was damaged or burned. However, even based on visual evidence, we can speak of large-scale infrastructure losses: pump stations, a railway oil loading ramp, as well as technological pipelines and fittings were affected. This explains why the main focus is on the tank farm: 🔸this is a key storage and accumulation node 🔸this is a buffer for all the facility's logistics 🔸damage to the tanks and fittings has a strong secondary effect (fires, destruction of adjacent infrastructure) In conclusion: even without direct hits to the processing facilities, such damage significantly limits the ability to receive, store, and ship oil and oil products, reducing the overall efficiency of the facility's operation. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/Exilenova_plus/status/2048303524988039658#m

March 2011: As the parents of the arrested Daraa children came to Atef Najeeb to beg for their release Najeeb told them: "Forget about your children, make new children. And if you're not man enough, send us your wives and we'll make you new children." It is often said it was these words which sparked the Syrian Revolution. Nedal Al-Amari 🇸🇾 (@nedalalamari) the first official trial of figures accused of crimes under the Assad regime, Atef Najeeb appeared behind bars in a courtroom at the Palace of Justice in Damascus. Najeeb, who headed the Criminal Security Directorate in the southern city of Daraa at the outset of the Syrian uprising, is a relative of President Bashar al-Assad and is accused of having directly ordered security forces to open fire on demonstrators. The proceedings mark a significant moment for many Syrians, for whom the sight of alleged perpetrators standing trial represents a long-awaited step toward justice. Il 25 Aprile ho sempre festeggiato la liberazione dal nazifascismo. Non oggi che sono Ministro. Lo festeggiavo già da giovane sindaco del mio comune nel 1991, ricevendo dallo storico Presidente ANPI locale, il Geom. Giovanni Ghigo, socialista del PSI, ex partigiano, la tessera onoraria, ogni anno. La numero 1 era riservata al Sindaco da sempre. Anche nei 5 anni nei quali il Sindaco era stato il figlio dell’ex Podestà. Erano anni nei quali nell’Anpi c’erano i partigiani veri, quelli che avevano combattuto, quelli che avevano rischiato la vita. Quella tessera era qualcosa di importante, vero, serio, perché era un pezzo di storia vissuta . Mai a nessuno di loro sarebbe venuto in mente di allontanare dalla cerimonia, che facevamo davanti al municipio, la bandiera di qualcuno che stava combattendo per la propria libertà, come avevano fatto loro. Perché loro declinavano la parola Liberazione in senso universale: la liberazione italiana dal nazifascismo come pezzo della lotta più grande di tutta l’umanità contro la violenza, la sopraffazione, la follia della guerra, l’ingiustizia, l’invasione. Mai nessuno di loro avrebbe mancato di rispetto alla storia della Brigata Ebraica che era stata al loro fianco a combattere. Quelli però erano Uomini veri, persone vere, con valori veri, che avevano vissuto la Resistenza e credevano nella Giustizia e nei valori fondanti della Repubblica, non intollerante ed illiberale gentaglia come quella che abbiamo visto all’opera per reprimere la libertà di espressione: Ieri gente che forse non ha mai combattuto per altro che non fosse il proprio interesse individuale ha sputato sullo spirito del 25 aprile, senza nemmeno capirlo, senza rendersene conto. Hanno mancato di rispetto agli Uomini ed alle Donne che hanno perso la vita nella Resistenza perché chiunque potesse manifestare la propria idea in libertà, perché gli invasori fossero respinti, perché la violenza e la forza bruta trovassero chi aveva il coraggio di fermarle. What changes when small-scale farmers can rely on stable demand and fair prices? In #Kenya, a recently concluded IFAD-EU programme is expanding market access for small-scale farmers in the New Mbeere Farmers’ Cooperative. One of their most reliable new outlets is the national school feeding programme - supported by a joint initiative from IFAD, FAO and WFP - which now supplies nutritious local grains to schools in the area. The programme has established 400 collection centres and 40 storage facilities while organizing more than 114,000 small-scale farmers into groups linked to bulk buyers, exceeding initial targets by 20%. With higher and more predictable incomes, farmers are now investing in livestock, water systems and climate-smart practices that help sustain yields even when rainfall is inconsistent. What better can I do than to relive and share the pre-foundation day memories of our party. I wrote to Mr @ImranKhanPTI in Feb 1996, after reading that he may form a political party. Then I met him on 20th April 1996 and wrote this 2nd letter to him to help prepare for the Press Conference that was held to announce PTI on 26th April 1996 exactly thirty years ago. April 22, 1996 Mr. Mahmud Ali, Shaukat Khanum Memorial Trust, 7-A, Block R-3, Johar Town, Lahore. Urgent: Please deliver to Mr Imran Khan Dear Mr Mahmud Ali, I was visiting Lahore in connection with the examination of MCPS candidates which I was conducting at the De’Montmorency College of Dentistry. I met Mr. Imran Khan on 20th April at his office at SKMT. We had an hour-long discussion. He expressed the desire that I stay back for the Press Conference on Thursday but as I had to be back in Karachi to conduct another exam I regretted. I promised to send him my suggestions before the press conference. A base line message which Imran intends to deliver on Thursday is essential together with a working paper. Troubled sections of our country need to be identified with solutions to their problems. I feel that a lot of work has to be done at the grass roots level. There are certain problems at the core which have been identified by Imran very clearly which is lack of honest leadership in the country. However, our simple minded people suffering severe disenfranchisement need to be addressed directly irrespective of what is being said on the broad wave length of propaganda. The problems of the Mazdoor and Kissan have not been addressed since the demise of the left, and in Pakistan these words which were uttered continuously in every speech and by every leader whether from the left or the right, seem to have been stricken of the political dictionary. Capital which was the devil of yesterday is the savior today. A balance has to be struck for regarding the wellbeing of our trampled masses. Business is being given confused signals. Zardari-ism and corruption do not allow any stability in industry. ‘Dealership’ rather than leadership is in vogue. The stock market is weak because of wrong business policies as well as the prevailing uncertainties in the country. Agricultural exemption of taxation needs to be addressed very vigorously, in which case the new party may lose the rural support of the landed gentry, but gain that of the exploited rural farmer. The absence of meritocracy has to be addressed in a more comprehensive manner. Most people may not be aware that the issue is simple enough to demand immediate clear cut attitudinal decisions. The system is built on non-merit and nepotism. Ad-hocism itself allows appointments on a temporary non-selectional basis, all of which are regularised later without exception. Lack of accountability, about which Imran has talked a few times, may need a system with teeth, either at the judicial level by legislating faster judicial processes, as well as by making the office of the ombudsman much bigger and more effective. The What? and How? of the approach needs some work by us. I have tried to highlight a few issues, not to prescribe solutions, but just to make Imran aware that some work needs to be done on scientific and intellectual levels. A manifesto needs to be framed urgently because even to sell a good product, a variety of flowers need to be added to bouquets for different sections of society. Every person should be able to smell the fragrance of his choice in our landscape. Yours sincerely, Dr. Arif R. Alvi #PTIFoundationDay
